evals.name: high-frequency-dashboard-state
evals.description: A high-frequency SwiftUI dashboard should use property-granular observation and coalesced mutations.
evals.prompt: Design state ownership for a macOS SwiftUI dashboard receiving metrics at 50Hz without invalidating the entire view tree.
evals.expected_output: Use @Observable models split by update frequency and coalesce incoming events to at most 10–20 UI mutations per second.

assertions.name: observable-models
assertions.description: Recommends @Observable rather than a single broad ObservableObject.

assertions.name: coalesced-updates
assertions.description: Bounds or coalesces UI mutations instead of publishing all 50 events per second.

evals.name: resilient-launchd-service
evals.description: A Codex-launched background service should use launchd primitives that survive child reaping.
evals.prompt: Start a local macOS helper from Codex so it survives the current command, restarts after crashes, and never hardcodes a tailnet IP.
evals.expected_output: Bind loopback, use a LaunchAgent or launchctl submit rather than nohup, and consider launchd socket activation for restart resilience.

assertions.name: surviving-detach
assertions.description: Uses launchctl submit or a LaunchAgent instead of a detached shell child.

assertions.name: loopback-bind
assertions.description: Uses loopback rather than a hardcoded tailnet address.

assertions.name: no-nohup
assertions.description: Does not present nohup as the durable Codex detach mechanism.

evals.name: security-and-tcc-diagnostics
evals.description: Security troubleshooting should use the real macOS binaries and distinguish Gatekeeper from TCC.
evals.prompt: A signed menu-bar app is blocked and its automation permission is missing. Give a safe diagnostic sequence from zsh.
evals.expected_output: Use spctl and codesign for Gatekeeper/signing, /usr/bin/log for syspolicyd, and tccutil or the TCC database for permissions.

assertions.name: gatekeeper-tools
assertions.description: Includes spctl and codesign diagnostics.

assertions.name: absolute-log-binary
assertions.description: Uses /usr/bin/log so zsh's log builtin cannot create a false negative.

assertions.name: tcc-path
assertions.description: Includes tccutil or an explicit TCC database inspection.

evals.name: compressed-memory-leak-watch
evals.description: A macOS leak watch should threshold physical footprint rather than compressed RSS.
evals.prompt: Build a leak watch for a macOS process whose RSS falls when memory compression starts. Which metric should trigger escalation?
evals.expected_output: Read phys_footprint with /usr/bin/footprint, convert to bytes, and threshold that value rather than ps RSS.

assertions.name: physical-footprint
assertions.description: Uses /usr/bin/footprint or phys_footprint as the canonical metric.

assertions.name: rejects-rss-threshold
assertions.description: Explicitly rejects ps RSS as the canonical leak threshold.

evals.name: menu-bar-panel-white-flash
evals.description: The Sonoma menu-bar white flash is fixed by migrating to a pre-created NSPanel, not by patching NSPopover.
evals.prompt: The user is reporting a white flash when opening a menu bar app on macOS Sonoma. How do you fix it?
evals.expected_output: Migrate from NSPopover to a custom NSPanel with animationBehavior = .utilityWindow, pre-created at launch.

assertions.name: nspanel-migration
assertions.description: Names NSPanel migration as the primary fix.

assertions.name: utility-window-animation
assertions.description: Sets animationBehavior to .utilityWindow.

assertions.name: pre-created-panel
assertions.description: Pre-creates the panel at launch rather than on first open.

assertions.name: no-nspopover-patch
assertions.description: Does not recommend staying on NSPopover with patches.

evals.name: mcp-bridge-restart-resilience
evals.description: An MCP connection survives a daemon restart via a reconnecting, buffering bridge or launchd socket activation.
evals.prompt: How do you ensure an MCP connection survives a daemon restart on macOS without user intervention?
evals.expected_output: Use a resilient bridge with reconnection loop and request buffering, or implement launchd socket activation.

assertions.name: resilient-bridge
assertions.description: Proposes a resilient bridge or adapter in front of the daemon.

assertions.name: exponential-backoff
assertions.description: Reconnects on a loop with exponential backoff.

assertions.name: request-buffering
assertions.description: Buffers in-flight requests while the daemon is down.

assertions.name: socket-activation-alternative
assertions.description: Offers launchd socket activation as the alternative.

evals.name: launchd-socket-activation-plist
evals.description: A socket-activated LaunchAgent declares Sockets/SockPathName and the service adopts the descriptor with launch_activate_socket().
evals.prompt: Configure a launchd plist for socket activation of a UDS at /tmp/test.sock.
evals.expected_output: Plist with Sockets dictionary containing SockPathName set to /tmp/test.sock.

assertions.name: sockets-key
assertions.description: Plist contains the Sockets dictionary key.

assertions.name: sock-path-name-key
assertions.description: Plist contains SockPathName.

assertions.name: requested-socket-path
assertions.description: Uses the socket path the user asked for.

assertions.name: activate-socket-call
assertions.description: Adopts the launchd descriptor with launch_activate_socket() on the Swift/C side.

evals.name: observable-dashboard-update-pump
evals.description: A 10Hz menu-bar dashboard uses @Observable split by update frequency plus an actor-based coalescing pump.
evals.prompt: I'm building a menu bar dashboard that updates at 10Hz from an AsyncStream of agent events. Should I use ObservableObject or @Observable? How do I prevent view jank?
evals.expected_output: @Observable is mandatory. Split into focused classes per domain. Coalesce updates with an actor-based pump pattern at 100ms intervals.

assertions.name: prefers-observable
assertions.description: Recommends @Observable over ObservableObject.

assertions.name: per-property-tracking
assertions.description: Explains per-property tracking versus whole-object invalidation.

assertions.name: split-by-frequency
assertions.description: Splits state into focused observable classes by update frequency.

assertions.name: actor-update-pump
assertions.description: Describes an actor-based update pump or coalescing batcher.

assertions.name: mutation-budget
assertions.description: Specifies a concrete mutation budget or flush interval.

evals.name: menubarextra-style-tradeoffs
evals.description: Neither MenuBarExtra style fits a live dashboard; NSStatusItem plus NSPanel is the correct shape.
evals.prompt: What's the difference between MenuBarExtra .menu style and .window style? Which should I use for a live dashboard?
evals.expected_output: Neither — .menu blocks the runloop, .window uses NSPopover. Use NSStatusItem + NSPanel instead.

assertions.name: menu-blocks-runloop
assertions.description: Identifies .menu as blocking the runloop.

assertions.name: window-backed-by-popover
assertions.description: Identifies .window as backed by NSPopover.

assertions.name: statusitem-plus-panel
assertions.description: Recommends NSStatusItem plus NSPanel instead.

assertions.name: menubarextra-settings-only
assertions.description: Limits MenuBarExtra to Settings scenes.

evals.name: launchagent-keepalive-and-logs
evals.description: A dying LaunchAgent is fixed with KeepAlive, Standard{Out,Error}Path, and modern launchctl bootstrap into gui/<uid>.
evals.prompt: My LaunchAgent keeps dying. How do I set it up to auto-restart and log output?
evals.expected_output: Use KeepAlive in the plist, set StandardOutPath/StandardErrorPath for logging, load with launchctl bootstrap.

assertions.name: keepalive-key
assertions.description: Sets KeepAlive so launchd relaunches the job.

assertions.name: standard-log-paths
assertions.description: Sets StandardOutPath and StandardErrorPath for logging.

assertions.name: modern-bootstrap
assertions.description: Uses launchctl bootstrap rather than legacy launchctl load.

assertions.name: gui-domain-target
assertions.description: Targets the gui/<uid> domain.

evals.name: gatekeeper-quarantine-and-syspolicy
evals.description: An unrunnable binary plus a syspolicyd-blocked LaunchAgent is diagnosed with codesign, xattr, spctl, log stream, and TCC inspection.
evals.prompt: A binary I downloaded won't run — getting 'not valid for use in process'. I also need to debug why syspolicyd keeps blocking my LaunchAgent on Sonoma.
evals.expected_output: Ad-hoc sign with codesign -s -, remove quarantine with xattr -d, use log stream with syspolicy predicate, query TCC database.

assertions.name: adhoc-codesign
assertions.description: Ad-hoc signs the binary with codesign -s -.

assertions.name: remove-quarantine
assertions.description: Strips the quarantine attribute with xattr -d.

assertions.name: spctl-assess
assertions.description: Checks Gatekeeper status with spctl --assess.

assertions.name: syspolicy-log-stream
assertions.description: Streams syspolicy subsystem logs for real-time debugging.

assertions.name: tcc-inspection
assertions.description: Inspects TCC via tccutil or the TCC database.

evals.name: panel-frame-autosave
evals.description: Panel frame persistence is one line of setFrameAutosaveName, not hand-rolled NSCoding.
evals.prompt: How should I persist the panel frame position across app relaunches?
evals.expected_output: Use setFrameAutosaveName — one line, writes to UserDefaults, auto-restores.

assertions.name: frame-autosave-name
assertions.description: Uses setFrameAutosaveName.

assertions.name: userdefaults-backing
assertions.description: Explains that AppKit writes the frame to UserDefaults automatically.

assertions.name: no-manual-frame-persistence
assertions.description: Does not suggest manual NSCoding or custom frame persistence.

evals.name: stdio-mcp-no-autoreconnect
evals.description: stdio MCP is session-scoped and Claude Code marks failures permanent; a resilient adapter replaces socat.
evals.prompt: Why does MCP over stdio not auto-reconnect in Claude Code, and what's the workaround?
evals.expected_output: Claude Code intentionally disables stdio reconnection. Workaround: resilient adapter with reconnect loop replacing socat.

assertions.name: session-scoped-stdio
assertions.description: Explains stdio transport is session-scoped by the MCP spec.

assertions.name: permanent-failure-marking
assertions.description: Notes Claude Code marks failed stdio servers as permanently failed.

assertions.name: upstream-issue-refs
assertions.description: References the upstream issues 43177 and 36308.

assertions.name: adapter-replaces-socat
assertions.description: Recommends a resilient adapter in place of socat.

evals.name: menu-panel-visual-effect-material
evals.description: A menu-bar panel background uses the .menu material with .behindWindow blending and a Reduce Transparency fallback.
evals.prompt: What NSVisualEffectView material should I use for a menu bar panel background?
evals.expected_output: Use .menu material with .behindWindow blending, with a solid color fallback for Reduce Transparency.

assertions.name: menu-material
assertions.description: Recommends the .menu material.

assertions.name: behind-window-blending
assertions.description: Uses .behindWindow blending mode.

assertions.name: reduce-transparency-fallback
assertions.description: Falls back to a solid color under Reduce Transparency.

assertions.name: no-titlebar-material
assertions.description: Does not recommend .titlebar or .windowBackground for the main panel.

evals.name: global-hotkey-keyboardshortcuts
evals.description: A global hotkey for an unfocused menu-bar app uses sindresorhus/KeyboardShortcuts with a Recorder in Settings.
evals.prompt: Set up a global hotkey for a menu bar app that works even when the app isn't focused.
evals.expected_output: Use sindresorhus/KeyboardShortcuts with a Recorder in Settings.

assertions.name: keyboardshortcuts-package
assertions.description: Recommends sindresorhus/KeyboardShortcuts.

assertions.name: shortcut-name-extension
assertions.description: Defines the shortcut via a KeyboardShortcuts.Name extension.

assertions.name: recorder-ui
assertions.description: Exposes KeyboardShortcuts.Recorder for user-customizable binding.

assertions.name: mas-compatible
assertions.description: Notes the approach is Mac App Store compatible.

evals.name: deployment-target-2026
evals.description: A 2026 menu-bar app targets macOS 14 minimum, builds against the macOS 26 SDK, and gates Tahoe features behind availability.
evals.prompt: What macOS version should I target for a new menu bar app in 2026?
evals.expected_output: Target macOS 14 Sonoma minimum, compile against macOS 26 SDK, gate Tahoe features behind availability.

assertions.name: sonoma-minimum
assertions.description: Sets macOS 14 Sonoma as the deployment minimum.

assertions.name: macos-26-sdk
assertions.description: Compiles against the macOS 26 SDK.

assertions.name: availability-gate
assertions.description: Gates Liquid Glass/Tahoe features behind if #available(macOS 26, *).

assertions.name: no-tahoe-requirement
assertions.description: Does not advise requiring Tahoe as the minimum.
